evidence.title: Belleville, Illinois
evidence.text: Belleville (French: "Belle ville", meaning "Beautiful city") is a city in St. Clair County, Illinois, United States, coterminous with the now defunct Belleville Township.

evidence.title: Belleville, Illinois
evidence.text: The population was 42,034 according to the Census Bureau's 2015 estimates.

evidence.title: Belleville, Illinois
evidence.text: It is the eighth-most populated city outside the Chicago Metropolitan Area and the most populated city south of Springfield in the state of Illinois.

evidence.title: Belleville, Illinois
evidence.text: It is the county seat of St. Clair County, and the seat of the Roman Catholic Diocese of Belleville and the National Shrine of Our Lady of the Snows.

evidence.title: Belleville, Illinois
evidence.text: Belleville is the most populated city in the Metro-East region of the St. Louis Metropolitan Area and in Southern Illinois.

evidence.title: Belleville, Illinois
evidence.text: Due to its proximity to Scott Air Force Base, the population receives a boost from military and federal civilian personnel, defense contractors, and military retirees.

evidence.title: Lake Hancock
evidence.text: Lake Hancock is a lake located north of Bartow, Florida in Polk County, Florida.

evidence.title: Lake Hancock
evidence.text: Lake Hancock is located in the Polk Upland area between the Winter Haven Ridge and Lakeland Ridge.

evidence.title: Lake Hancock
evidence.text: As part of the upper Peace River watershed, the lake has ecological importance throughout southwest Florida according to the Southwest Florida Water Management District.

evidence.title: Lake Hancock
evidence.text: Lake Hancock is shallow with an average depth of four feet and a maximum depth of 16 ft .

evidence.title: Lake Hancock
evidence.text: At 4573 acre , the lake is one of the largest lakes in Polk County, Florida; the center of the cities of Bartow, Lakeland, and Winter Haven roughly form an equilateral triangle with sides of 12 mi and Lake Hancock forms over 25% of that triangle.

evidence.title: Lake Hancock
evidence.text: The first settlements in the area occurred in 1849 when small farms were established in the area as a result of migration from a hurricane in the Tampa Bay area.

evidence.title: Eagle Ridge Mall
evidence.text: Eagle Ridge Mall is a regional, enclosed shopping mall located on the north side of Lake Wales, Florida.

evidence.title: Eagle Ridge Mall
evidence.text: This mall has two anchor stores: JCPenney and Dillard's.

evidence.title: Eagle Ridge Mall
evidence.text: It also has a Regal Cinemas, which has twelve theatres, and a large entertainment center, which contains a bowling alley, a large video arcade, a restaurant and meeting rooms.

evidence.title: Eagle Ridge Mall
evidence.text: On the north side of the mall is a large food court and a carousel.

evidence.title: Eagle Ridge Mall
evidence.text: Sears relocated from an existing mall, Winter Haven Mall, in nearby Winter Haven.

evidence.title: April 1958 Florida tornado outbreak
evidence.text: The April 1958 Florida tornado outbreak was a severe weather event that primarily affected the Florida peninsula on April 15, 1958.

evidence.title: April 1958 Florida tornado outbreak
evidence.text: A total of five tornadoes touched down in the state of Georgia between 12–5 p.m. EST.

evidence.title: April 1958 Florida tornado outbreak
evidence.text: 80 percent of the tornadoes were recorded in Florida, while 75 percent of the Florida events attained F3 intensity or greater.

evidence.title: April 1958 Florida tornado outbreak
evidence.text: The strongest tornado produced F4 damage on the Fujita scale in Polk County, Florida, becoming one of only two F4 tornadoes recorded in the U.S. state of Florida.

evidence.title: April 1958 Florida tornado outbreak
evidence.text: The second F4 tornado occurred on April 4, 1966, in Polk County near Gibsonia and Galloway.

evidence.title: April 1958 Florida tornado outbreak
evidence.text: In total, 65–72 people were injured during the 1958 outbreak, but no deaths were directly related to the tornadoes.

evidence.title: April 1958 Florida tornado outbreak
evidence.text: In addition to confirmed tornadoes, an unconfirmed tornado was also reported near Wimauma, Florida.

evidence.title: Livingston, Texas
evidence.text: Livingston is a city in and the county seat of Polk County, Texas, United States.

evidence.title: Livingston, Texas
evidence.text: With a population of 5,335 at the 2010 census, it is the largest city in Polk County.

evidence.title: Livingston, Texas
evidence.text: It is located approximately seventy-five miles north of Houston and was originally settled in 1835 as Springfield.

evidence.title: Livingston, Texas
evidence.text: Its name was changed to Livingston and became the county seat of Polk County in 1846.

evidence.title: Lakeland Square Mall
evidence.text: Lakeland Square Mall is a shopping mall located on the northern side of Lakeland, Florida in the United States.

evidence.title: Lakeland Square Mall
evidence.text: It is one of two enclosed malls serving Polk County.

evidence.title: Lakeland Square Mall
evidence.text: It is owned and managed by Rouse Properties, one of the largest mall owners in the United States.

evidence.title: Lakeland Square Mall
evidence.text: It is the only shopping mall located off of I-4 between Tampa and Orlando, and it serves the populations of western Polk County.

evidence.title: Winter Haven, Florida
evidence.text: Winter Haven is a city in Polk County, Florida, United States.

evidence.title: Winter Haven, Florida
evidence.text: The population was 33,874 at the 2010 census.

evidence.title: Winter Haven, Florida
evidence.text: According to the U.S. Census Bureau's 2015 estimates, the city had a population of 37,689, making it the second most populated city in Polk County.

evidence.title: Winter Haven, Florida
evidence.text: It is a principal city of the Lakeland-Winter Haven, Florida Metropolitan Statistical Area.

evidence.title: Tenoroc High School
evidence.text: Tenoroc High School (THS) is a public secondary school in Lakeland, Florida.

evidence.title: Tenoroc High School
evidence.text: The current principal is Jason Looney, and is assisted by four Assistant principals, Bradley Hardesty, Haley Mason, Summer Fisher and Brandi Blanchard.

evidence.title: Tenoroc High School
evidence.text: The School Board of Polk County established Tenoroc to relieve overcrowding problems at Lakeland High School, Lake Gibson High School, Auburndale High School, and Lake Region High School.

evidence.title: Tenoroc High School
evidence.text: It is also one of the more technologically advanced schools owned by the School Board of Polk County and hosts a specialized learning center known as "Power Academy."

evidence.title: Tenoroc High School
evidence.text: Power Academy is a 4-year training program for students intending to be employed at Lakeland Electric, Polk County's municipal utility company.

evidence.title: Ridge Community High School
evidence.text: Ridge Community High School or RCHS is a public high school located on the Davenport, Florida and Haines City, Florida Line.

evidence.title: Ridge Community High School
evidence.text: RCHS was established in 2005 in Polk County.

evidence.title: Ridge Community High School
evidence.text: It currently serves 2,600 students and has 106 teachers on campus.

evidence.title: Ridge Community High School
evidence.text: Ridge Community High School is one of many schools with a separate 9th Grade campus with its own front office.

evidence.title: Ridge Community High School
evidence.text: The main campus holds students in 10th, 11th, and 12th grade with some exceptions.

evidence.title: Ridge Community High School
evidence.text: Ridge Community High School sits on 76 acre of land.

evidence.title: Ridge Community High School
evidence.text: Ridge Community High School is zoned for Davenport and Haines City.

evidence.title: Ridge Community High School
evidence.text: Ridge Community High School's rivals include Haines City High School, Lake Wales High School and others in Polk County.

evidence.title: Ridge Community High School
evidence.text: The principal of RCHS is currently Russell Donnelly who replaced Sherry Wells, the acting principal between the school's opening in 2005 and 2015 and has a few assistant principals.

evidence.title: Ridge Community High School
evidence.text: Ridge Community High School is part of the Polk County School Board.

evidence.title: Ridge Community High School
evidence.text: RCHS's mascot is the Bolt, and the school motto is Once a Bolt, always a Bolt.

evidence.title: Lakeland, Florida
evidence.text: Lakeland is a city in Polk County, Florida, located along Interstate 4 east of Tampa.

evidence.title: Lakeland, Florida
evidence.text: It is generally considered part of the Tampa Bay Area.

evidence.title: Lakeland, Florida
evidence.text: According to the 2013 U.S. Census Bureau estimate, the city had a population of 100,710.

evidence.title: Lakeland, Florida
evidence.text: Lakeland is a principal city of the Lakeland–Winter Haven Metropolitan Statistical Area (coterminous with Polk County), which had an estimated population of 623,009 in July 2013 based on data from the University of Florida Bureau of Economic and Business Research.

evidence.title: Lakeland, Florida
evidence.text: It is twinned with Richmond Hill, Ontario; Imabari, Ehime, Japan; Bălți, Moldova; Portmore, Jamaica; and Chongming County, Shanghai, China through the Lakeland chapter of Sister Cities International.
